title: SAGA: Domain-Matched Predictor Adaptation and Off-the-Shelf Audio-Visual Synchrony Scoring for Deepfake Attribution
description: Cross-modal prediction residuals from frozen audio-visual predictors trained only on real content have been proposed for zero-shot deepfake attribution, without any fake training data. We show this signal is highly sensitive to an uncontrolled factor: domain match between the corpus used to adapt the predictors and the evaluation data. A mismatched adaptation corpus collapses attribution to near chance; adapting on the evaluation dataset's own real clips restores it, an effect verified bidirectionally between FakeAVCeleb and LAV-DF (Random Forest AUC: 69.1 versus 66.4 percent in- versus out-of-domain on FakeAVCeleb, 55.4 versus 48.1 percent on LAV-DF). We then test whether an off-the-shelf, zero-training synchrony scorer (SyncNet) adds complementary signal. It substantially improves closed-set attribution (AUC 69.1 to 73.3 percent, macro F1 33.4 to 43.3 percent) but consistently reduces open-set AUROC for an unseen generator, a tradeoff replicated across three classifiers and explained mechanistically. Notably, Logistic Regression outperforms both Random Forest and a purpose-built temporal BiLSTM on closed-set and identity-disjoint protocols, with one notable exception to the tradeoff that we report rather than omit. We evaluate across four protocols, random-split, identity-disjoint, and two open-set generator hold-outs, and recommend deployment configurations for each. This record archives the reference implementation (code only); the datasets (FakeAVCeleb, DF-TIMIT, LAV-DF) are not redistributed.
